name: MK20DX128VFM5
title: Kinetis K20 32-pin 50 MHz Cortex-M4 microcontroller with USB OTG
summary: A family of 50 MHz ARM Cortex-M4 microcontrollers with DSP instructions, 32 KB to 128 KB of flash, up to 16 KB of RAM and a full-speed USB On-the-Go controller with its own transceiver and 3.3 V regulator, in a 5 mm square 32-pin QFN. The DX parts add FlexMemory for EEPROM emulation. A 16-bit ADC, two comparators, touch sensing, timers, SPI, I2C, two UARTs and I2S share the 20 port pins. It runs from 1.71 V to 3.6 V over -40 °C to 105 °C.
key_figures: ARM Cortex-M4 with DSP, 50 MHz max
up to 32 KB FlexNVM, 2 KB FlexRAM
13.9 mA typ at 50 MHz, 3.0 V, peripherals off

pins.name: VDD
pins.function: Digital supply, 1.71 V to 3.6 V.

pins.name: VSS
pins.function: Digital ground.

pins.name: USB0_DP
pins.function: USB full/low-speed data plus line of the on-chip transceiver; input range -0.3 V to 3.63 V.

pins.name: USB0_DM
pins.function: USB data minus line of the on-chip transceiver; input range -0.3 V to 3.63 V.

pins.name: VOUT33
pins.function: Output of the internal USB voltage regulator, 3.3 V typical in run mode; takes 1.76 µF to 8.16 µF with ESR 1 mΩ to 100 mΩ to ground.

pins.name: VREGIN
pins.function: Input of the USB voltage regulator, 2.7 V to 5.5 V operating, 6.0 V absolute maximum.

pins.name: VDDA
pins.function: Analog supply, 1.71 V to 3.6 V; within 100 mV of VDD.

pins.name: VSSA
pins.function: Analog ground; within 100 mV of VSS.

pins.name: XTAL32
pins.function: Output side of the 32.768 kHz oscillator; left open when EXTAL32 takes an external clock.

pins.name: EXTAL32
pins.function: Input side of the 32.768 kHz oscillator, or an external 32.768 kHz clock input.

pins.name: VBAT
pins.function: Battery supply for the RTC, 32 kHz oscillator and VBAT register file, 1.71 V to 3.6 V.

pins.name: PTA0
pins.function: Port A0. Comes out of reset as JTAG TCLK / SWD clock (EzPort clock in EzPort mode); also touch channel 1, UART0 CTS/COL, FTM0 channel 5.

pins.name: PTA1
pins.function: Port A1. Default JTAG TDI (EzPort data in); also touch channel 2, UART0 RX, FTM0 channel 6.

pins.name: PTA2
pins.function: Port A2. Default JTAG TDO / trace SWO (EzPort data out); also touch channel 3, UART0 TX, FTM0 channel 7.

pins.name: PTA3
pins.function: Port A3. Default JTAG TMS / SWD data; also touch channel 4, UART0 RTS, FTM0 channel 0.

pins.name: PTA4/LLWU_P3
pins.function: Port A4 and wakeup source LLWU_P3. Default non-maskable interrupt input; EzPort chip select, sampled after reset to choose EzPort mode; also touch channel 5, FTM0 channel 1.

pins.name: PTA18
pins.function: Port A18. Default EXTAL0, input of the 3 MHz to 32 MHz main oscillator or an external clock; also FTM0 fault 2, FTM clock input 0.

pins.name: PTA19
pins.function: Port A19. Default XTAL0, output of the main oscillator; also FTM1 fault 0, FTM clock input 1, LPTMR0 alternate input 1.

pins.name: RESET_b
pins.function: Active-low reset.

pins.name: PTB0/LLWU_P5
pins.function: Port B0 and wakeup source LLWU_P5. Default ADC0 single-ended input 8 / touch channel 0; also I2C0 SCL, FTM1 channel 0, FTM1 quadrature phase A.

pins.name: PTB1
pins.function: Port B1. Default ADC0 single-ended input 9 / touch channel 6; also I2C0 SDA, FTM1 channel 1, FTM1 quadrature phase B.

pins.name: PTC1/LLWU_P6
pins.function: Port C1 and wakeup source LLWU_P6. Default ADC0 input 15 / touch channel 14; also SPI0 PCS3, UART1 RTS, FTM0 channel 0, I2S0 transmit data.

pins.name: PTC2
pins.function: Port C2. Default ADC0 input 4b / CMP1 input 0 / touch channel 15; also SPI0 PCS2, UART1 CTS, FTM0 channel 1, I2S0 transmit frame sync.

pins.name: PTC3/LLWU_P7
pins.function: Port C3 and wakeup source LLWU_P7. Default CMP1 input 1; also SPI0 PCS1, UART1 RX, FTM0 channel 2, I2S0 transmit bit clock.

pins.name: PTC4/LLWU_P8
pins.function: Port C4 and wakeup source LLWU_P8. Disabled after reset; SPI0 PCS0, UART1 TX, FTM0 channel 3, CMP1 output.

pins.name: PTC5/LLWU_P9
pins.function: Port C5 and wakeup source LLWU_P9. Disabled after reset; SPI0 SCK, LPTMR0 alternate input 2, I2S0 receive data, CMP0 output.

pins.name: PTC6/LLWU_P10
pins.function: Port C6 and wakeup source LLWU_P10. Default CMP0 input 0; also SPI0 SOUT, PDB0 external trigger, I2S0 receive bit clock, I2S0 master clock.

pins.name: PTC7
pins.function: Port C7. Default CMP0 input 1; also SPI0 SIN, USB start-of-frame output, I2S0 receive frame sync.

pins.name: PTD4/LLWU_P14
pins.function: Port D4 and wakeup source LLWU_P14. Disabled after reset; SPI0 PCS1, UART0 RTS, FTM0 channel 4, watchdog monitor input.

pins.name: PTD5
pins.function: Port D5. Default ADC0 input 6b; also SPI0 PCS2, UART0 CTS/COL, FTM0 channel 5, watchdog monitor output.

pins.name: PTD6/LLWU_P15
pins.function: Port D6 and wakeup source LLWU_P15. Default ADC0 input 7b; also SPI0 PCS3, UART0 RX, FTM0 channel 6, FTM0 fault 0.

pins.name: PTD7
pins.function: Port D7. Disabled after reset; CMT infrared output, UART0 TX, FTM0 channel 7, FTM0 fault 1.

operation.text: The six parts are each an ARM Cortex-M4 with DSP instructions at up to 50 MHz (1.25 Dhrystone MIPS per MHz), 32, 64 or 128 KB of program flash, and up to 16 KB of SRAM. The DX parts add FlexMemory: up to 32 KB of FlexNVM and 2 KB of FlexRAM, which together give EEPROM emulation of selectable size. All run from 1.71 V to 3.6 V, flash writes included, over -40 °C to 105 °C ambient, in a 5 mm x 5 mm 32-pin QFN.

Hardware CRC, a 128-bit unique ID, a 16-bit SAR ADC, two comparators each with a 6-bit DAC and programmable reference, a programmable delay block, an eight-channel FlexTimer for motor control and PWM, a two-channel FlexTimer with quadrature decoding, periodic interrupt timers, a 16-bit low-power timer, a carrier modulator transmitter, an RTC, a full/low-speed USB On-the-Go controller with on-chip transceiver and 3.3 V regulator, one SPI, one I2C, two UARTs and one I2S. A four-channel DMA controller serves up to 41 request sources. An external watchdog monitor, a software watchdog, a low-leakage wakeup unit and a touch-sensing interface complete the set; EzPort gives serial programming of the flash.

Clock sources are a 3 MHz to 32 MHz crystal oscillator on EXTAL0/XTAL0, a 32 kHz oscillator on EXTAL32/XTAL32 powered from VBAT, and the multi-purpose clock generator, which holds a slow (32.768 kHz trimmed) and a fast (4 MHz) internal reference, an FLL and a PLL with a 48 MHz to 100 MHz VCO. Full-speed USB needs the system clock at 20 MHz or more.

EXTAL0 and XTAL0 carry only the crystal or resonator and its load parts. Load capacitance can come from the on-chip capacitors or external ones, valued to the crystal vendor's figures. In low-power mode (HGO=0) the feedback resistor is internal and no external one may be fitted; high-gain mode uses 10 MΩ (low-frequency) or 1 MΩ (high-frequency) feedback with a 200 kΩ series resistor in low-frequency high-gain mode. The 32 kHz oscillator has a 100 MΩ internal feedback resistor; EXTAL32 can instead take an external 32.768 kHz clock of at least 700 mV peak-to-peak within VSS to VBAT, with XTAL32 left open.

Beyond Run and Wait there are very-low-power run and wait (VLPR, VLPW, clocks limited to 4 MHz core and bus, 1 MHz flash), Stop, very-low-power stop (VLPS), low-leakage stop (LLS) and very-low-leakage stops VLLS3 to VLLS0. Recovery to Run takes up to 5.2 µs from STOP or VLPS, 6 µs from LLS, 70 µs from VLLS3 and VLLS2 and 130 µs from VLLS1 and VLLS0. Wakeup sources LLWU_Px sit on PTA4, PTB0, PTC1, PTC3 to PTC6, PTD4 and PTD6. The VBAT supply runs the RTC and 32 kHz oscillator and holds the VBAT register file; with the RTC running it draws 0.57 µA typical at 1.8 V and 0.67 µA typical at 3.0 V, -40 °C to 25 °C.

POR trips as VDD falls through about 1.1 V (0.8 V to 1.5 V). After POR, code starts within 300 µs of VDD reaching 1.71 V. The low-voltage detector has a high range (2.56 V trip, LVDV=01) and a low range (1.60 V trip, LVDV=00), each with four warning levels 100 mV apart set by LVWV; rising thresholds sit one hysteresis above the falling ones. RAM is held down to VDD = 1.2 V.

Port pins drive 9 mA (high drive) or 2 mA (low drive) at 2.7 V to 3.6 V within 0.5 V of the rail, with at most 100 mA total sourced and 100 mA total sunk across all ports and 25 mA on any one pin. Pull-ups and pull-downs are 22 kΩ to 50 kΩ. Analog pins clamp to VSS and VDD through ESD diodes; within VSS - 0.3 V to VDD + 0.3 V no series resistor is needed, otherwise one limits injection to 3 mA per pin and 25 mA per 16 neighbouring pins. PTC4, PTC5, PTD4 and PTD7 come out of reset disabled; the JTAG/SWD pins PTA0 to PTA3 and the NMI pin PTA4 come out of reset in those roles.

PTA4 serves as EZP_CS_b: its level is held for at least 2 bus clocks after reset deasserts to choose EzPort mode, in which PTA0, PTA1 and PTA2 become the EzPort clock, data in and data out. EzPort clocks up to fSYS/2 (fSYS/8 for READ). The debug port is JTAG (to 10 MHz TCLK) or cJTAG (to 5 MHz), with serial wire debug on PTA0 and PTA3 and trace SWO on PTA2.

VREGIN takes 2.7 V to 5.5 V and VOUT33 delivers 3.3 V typical, up to 120 mA in run mode and 1 mA in standby, with about 290 mA short-circuit current. Below 3.6 V in it passes the input through, less a load-dependent drop. VOUT33 needs 1.76 µF to 8.16 µF (2.2 µF typical) with 1 mΩ to 100 mΩ ESR. The USB data pins tolerate -0.3 V to 3.63 V. The USB DCD block sources 7 µA to 13 µA on USB_DP and sinks 50 µA to 150 µA on USB_DM.

The 16-bit accuracy figures apply to the differential pair ADCx_DP0/ADCx_DM0; every other channel reaches 13-bit differential or 12-bit single-ended accuracy. On this package the ADC0 inputs are SE4b, SE6b, SE7b, SE8, SE9 and SE15. The characteristics hold with VREFH = VDDA and VREFL = VSSA. Each input looks like a 2 kΩ typical series resistance into 8 pF (16-bit) or 4 pF sampling capacitance; the specified figures come from a source under 8 Ω, with the source RC under 1 ns. The conversion clock runs 2 MHz to 12 MHz in 16-bit modes and 1 MHz to 18 MHz otherwise, the top clock needing ADHSC set and ADLPC clear. An internal temperature sensor reads 719 mV at 25 °C with a 1.715 mV/°C slope.

Each comparator works from 1.71 V to 3.6 V with inputs from VSS - 0.3 V to VDD, up to 20 mV offset, hysteresis selectable at 5, 10, 20 or 30 mV typical, and 50 ns typical delay in high-speed mode (200 µA) or 250 ns in low-speed mode (20 µA). The hysteresis grows when the input nears either rail. A 6-bit DAC gives each comparator a reference in steps of Vreference/64.

When the FlexNVM partition is not all data flash, part of it backs the FlexRAM as EEPROM, and the built-in record manager spreads writes over that larger backup to raise endurance. Endurance rises with the ratio of backup to FlexRAM: from 35 K writes minimum at a ratio of 16 to 20 M at 8192, for byte writes. Only one partition and EEPROM size is meant to be used over the product's life.

SPI0 runs to 25 MHz as master and 12.5 MHz as slave with VDD from 2.7 V to 3.6 V, and to 12.5 MHz master and 6.25 MHz slave over the full 1.71 V to 3.6 V. I2C and UART timing follows the general switching table. I2S0 works as master or slave over the full supply range, with the master clock to 12.5 MHz and the bit clock to 4 MHz in VLPR.

The TSI measures electrodes of 1 pF to 500 pF (best performance inside that range) to 16-bit resolution, taking about 15 µs per measurement at 20 pF. It adds 55 µA in run mode and 1.3 µA typical in low-power mode. Touch channels on this package are TSI0_CH0 to CH6, CH14 and CH15.

32-pin QFN, 5 mm x 5 mm body, outline drawing 98ARE10566D. Moisture sensitivity level 3; lead-free solder peak 260 °C. Junction-to-ambient thermal resistance is 94 °C/W on a single-layer board and 32 °C/W on a four-layer board in still air; junction-to-case is 1.5 °C/W.
